mainTopic: Conception and birth אגדות, the end of פרק המפלת חתיכה, and the new משנה about כותים (נדה ל״א ע״ב)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching about having sons: men who hold back so their wives 'give seed' first are credited with many sons, and רבא adds another method. Next, רבי אמי and רבי יוחנן disagree about when a woman conceives, close to her period or close to her טבילה, each reading half of the same פסוק in תהלים. A string of אגדות follows: a boy brings peace and his own livelihood, while a girl comes empty-handed. The students of רבי שמעון בן יוחי ask why a יולדת brings a קרבן, why she is טמאה seven or fourteen days, and why מילה is on the eighth day. He explains all three through the oath she makes in labor, though רב יוסף challenges it. רבי מאיר explains the seven days of נדה as keeping a wife dear to her husband, and רבי דוסתאי explains differences between men and women from how each was created. Then פרק המפלת חתיכה ends, and a new משנה rules that daughters of כותים are נדות from the cradle and their men are בועלי נדות, though their impurity is only a ספק. The גמרא asks what case this means, רב ששת answers that it is an unknown case where we worry about the minority, and the גמרא begins asking which תנא holds that view. The answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Men who hold back are credited with many sons
steps.stepSummary: The end of an earlier דרשה. Men who delay so that their wives 'give seed' first have sons, and the פסוק credits them as if they 'multiply sons and grandsons.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they hold themselves back inside, so that their wives give seed first and their children will be boys, the פסוק counts it for them as if they are producing many sons and grandsons.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it began just before this section. It explains how a person can be described as 'having many sons' when that seems to be up to ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An earlier rule said that if the woman gives seed first, the child will be a boy. So a man who holds back lets that happen, and the פסוק credits him with the result. This shows a person can do something that affects whether his children are boys.

keyTerms.meaning: To give seed (here: the woman giving seed first)
The פסוק counts it for them as if...

phrases.english: that they hold themselves back inside
phrases.notes: This finishes explaining the פסוק about the sons of אולם (דברי הימים א 8:40), who 'multiply sons and grandsons.'

phrases.english: so that their wives give seed first,
so that their children will be boys —
the verse counts it for them

phrases.aramaic: כְּאִילּוּ הֵם מַרְבִּים בָּנִים וּבְנֵי בָּנִים.
phrases.english: as though they produce many sons and grandsons.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer begun before this section
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק credits these men with sons because they held back so their wives would give seed first.

steps.title: This matches what רב קטינא said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב קטינא's claim that he could make all his children boys rests on the same idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what רב קטינא meant when he said: I could make all my children boys.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the idea from step 1 to a known statement of רב קטינא, showing they are the same idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב קטינא's bold claim sounds strange by itself. Now we understand it: he meant he could hold back until his wife gave seed first. The two statements support each other.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as...

phrases.english: And this is what Rav Ketina said:
I could make all my children boys.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties a sage's statement to the idea just explained
steps.raayaObject: The idea that holding back leads to sons
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב קטינא's statement that he could make all his children boys

steps.title: רבא's method for having sons
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives another way to have sons: have relations and then repeat.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Someone who wants all his children to be boys should have relations and then do it a second time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second practical method for having boys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the same basic rule: if the woman gives seed first, the child is a boy. Repeating the act makes it more likely that her seed comes first the second time.

keyTerms.meaning: He should have relations and repeat it

phrases.english: Rava said:
One who wants to make all his children boys —
should have relations and repeat.

steps.whatToRemember: The whole section rests on one rule: if the woman gives seed first, the child is a boy. Holding back (step 1) and repeating (רבא) are two ways to make that happen.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הָרוֹצֶה לַעֲשׂוֹת כׇּל בָּנָיו זְכָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second method on the same theme
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To have sons, have relations and repeat.

steps.title: A woman conceives only close to her period
steps.stepSummary: A new topic. רבי יצחק in the name of רבי אמי says a woman becomes pregnant only from relations close to her expected period, based on 'הן בעוון חוללתי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי אמי: A woman becomes pregnant only close to the time of her period, as the פסוק says: 'Behold, I was formed in sin.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic: when is a woman able to conceive? רבי אמי says it is only near her expected period.
steps.deeperAnalysis: דוד המלך says he was formed 'in sin.' רבי אמי reads this as relations close to the time of the period, when relations are forbidden. So he concludes that conception happens at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: Close to the time of her expected period

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said, Rabbi Ami said:
A woman does not become pregnant
except close to her period,
as it says: "Behold, I was formed in sin."
phrases.notes: תהלים 51:7.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: אֵין אִשָּׁה מִתְעַבֶּרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Conception happens only from relations close to the woman's expected period.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: conception is close to her immersion
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees: a woman conceives close to her טבילה, based on the second half of the same פסוק, 'ובחטא יחמתני אמי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן said: close to her immersion, as the פסוק says: 'And in חטא my mother conceived me.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite timing: conception happens right after the woman goes to the מקוה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the next words in the same פסוק. He reads חטא not as 'sin' but as 'purity,' meaning the time right after she became טהורה through טבילה. This reading needs proof, and that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Immersion in a מקוה, which makes her טהורה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read חטא here as 'sin.' רבי יוחנן reads it as 'purity,' so the פסוק points to the time right after her טבילה, not to something forbidden.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said:
close to her immersion,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording, 'her immersion.' The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: as it says: "And in chet my mother conceived me."
phrases.notes: תהלים 51:7, the second half of the same פסוק.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי אמי about the timing
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Conception happens only from relations close to her immersion.

steps.title: How do we know חטא means purity?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source showing that the word חטא can mean 'purifying.'
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that this word 'חטא' is a term for purifying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to check רבי יוחנן's reading. It asks what shows that חטא can mean purity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's whole proof depends on reading חטא as 'purity,' which is not its usual meaning. Before accepting it, the גמרא wants a source for this meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: What shows / how do we know

phrases.english: From where is it shown
that this word "chet" is a term for purifying?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מַשְׁמַע דְּהַאי חֵטְא לִישָּׁנָא דְּדַכּוֹיֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רבי יוחנן's reading
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that חטא means purity

steps.title: Proof from the purifying of a house
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about a house with צרעת says 'וחטא את הבית,' and the תרגום translates it as 'he shall purify the house.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'וחטא את הבית,' and we translate it into Aramaic as 'and he shall purify the house.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about purifying a house that had צרעת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that פסוק, וחטא clearly means making the house טהור, and the Aramaic תרגום says this openly. So the same root can mean 'purity' in רבי יוחנן's פסוק too.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall purify the house

phrases.english: As it is written: "And he shall chitei the house,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:52, about a house that had צרעת.

phrases.english: and we translate it: "And he shall purify the house."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about חטא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In ויקרא, וחטא is translated as 'he shall purify.'

steps.title: Second proof: purge me with hyssop
steps.stepSummary: Another source: 'תחטאני באזוב ואטהר,' where חטא clearly goes together with becoming טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it from here: 'Purge me with hyssop and I will be pure.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second proof that חטא can mean purity, from a פסוק later in the same chapter of תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here תחטאני is directly followed by 'and I will be pure,' so it obviously means purifying. This proof is close to home, since it comes from the same מזמור as רבי יוחנן's פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
Hyssop, a plant used in purification

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי says conception happens near her period, from 'בעוון חוללתי.' רבי יוחנן says near her טבילה, from 'ובחטא,' reading חטא as purity. He backs this with וחטא את הבית and תחטאני באזוב.

phrases.english: And if you want, say it from here:
"Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be pure."
phrases.notes: תהלים 51:9.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative proof for the same point
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In תהלים, תחטאני appears next to ואטהר, showing that it means purify.

steps.title: When a boy is born, peace comes to the world
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק in the name of רבי אמי teaches that the birth of a זכר brings peace, using a wordplay: זכר = זה כר, a gift sent to a ruler.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי אמי: When a boy is born, peace comes into the world. The פסוק says 'Send a lamb (כר) to the ruler of the land,' and the word זכר can be read as 'this is a כר.'
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching from the same pair of רבי יצחק and רבי אמי. They say a baby boy brings peace into the world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is a wordplay. The letters of זכר are split into זה כר, 'this is a כר.' In ישעיהו, a כר is a gift sent to the ruler, and a gift like that keeps things peaceful.

keyTerms.meaning: A male, here a baby boy
A lamb, sent here as a gift to a ruler

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak said, Rabbi Ami said:
Once a male comes into the world,
peace comes into the world,
as it says: "Send a lamb to the ruler of the land."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 16:1

phrases.english: "Zachar" (male) means "this is a kar."
phrases.notes: It's a wordplay: זָכָר sounds like זֶה כַּר, so a boy is like that peace-bringing gift.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק, אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching from the same author as step 4, moving from conception to the birth of a boy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The birth of a זכר brings peace to the world, learned from the wordplay זכר = זה כר.

steps.title: A boy comes into the world with his loaf in hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק of the school of רבי אמי reads the same wordplay a different way: כר means food, so a boy arrives with his own livelihood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק from the school of רבי אמי said: When a boy is born, his loaf comes with him. זכר means 'this is a כר,' and כר means a meal, as the פסוק says 'he prepared a great meal (כרה) for them.'
steps.whatsHappening: A second teaching uses the same זה כר wordplay. This time it says a boy comes with his own food and livelihood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here כר is read as food, not as a gift to a ruler. The proof comes from מלכים ב, where כרה means a big meal. So a boy is able to provide for himself.

keyTerms.meaning: His loaf is in his hand, meaning he brings his own livelihood

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yitzchak of the school of Rabbi Ami said:
When a male comes into the world,
his loaf comes in his hand,
phrases.notes: His 'loaf' means his livelihood, what he will live on.

phrases.english: "Zachar" means "this is a kar,"
as it is written: "And he prepared a great meal for them."
phrases.notes: מלכים ב 6:23. Here כר is connected to food.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק דְּבֵי רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same wordplay as step 9 but gives כר a different meaning: food instead of a gift.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זכר comes into the world with his livelihood, since כר means a meal.

steps.title: A girl comes empty-handed and must ask for her needs
steps.stepSummary: In contrast, a נקבה comes with nothing (נקבה = נקייה באה), and she gets nothing until she asks, learned from לבן's words 'נקבה שכרך.'
steps.simpleTranslation: A girl, though, comes with nothing. נקבה can be read as 'she comes clean,' meaning empty. And until she says 'Give me my food,' people don't give it to her, as the פסוק says, 'Name your wages to me and I will give it.'
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the same teaching by contrasting a girl with a boy. It uses two wordplays on the word נקבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, נקבה is read as נקייה באה, 'she comes clean,' meaning with empty hands. Second, נקבה is linked to לבן's word נָקְבָה, 'state clearly.' He would pay יעקב only once יעקב stated his wages, so a girl must clearly ask for her food before she gets it.

keyTerms.meaning: A female, here a baby girl

steps.whatToRemember: Both teachings work by splitting a word into a phrase: זכר becomes זה כר (gift or food), and נקבה becomes נקייה באה (comes empty).

phrases.english: A female: nothing comes with her,
"Nekevah" means "she comes clean,"
phrases.notes: 'Clean' here means empty-handed: נְקֵבָה sounds like נְקִיָּיה בָּאָה.

phrases.english: until she says "My food!"
they do not give to her,
as it is written: "Name your wages to me, and I will give it."
phrases.notes: בראשית 30:28. לבן tells יעקב he will pay once יעקב clearly names his wages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 10's teaching by contrasting the girl with the boy.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נקבה comes without her own livelihood and receives support only once she asks for it.

steps.title: Why does a woman bring a קרבן after giving birth?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's students ask him why the תורה requires a יולדת to bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: The students of רבי שמעון בן יוחי asked him: Why did the תורה say that a woman who gave birth must bring a קרבן?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question is asked about birth. The students want to know the reason behind the יולדת's קרבן, and this sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires a קרבן after birth, and one of these is a חטאת, which usually comes for a sin. Giving birth is not a sin, so the students ask what the קרבן is for.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has given birth
An offering brought in the מקדש

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
For what reason did the Torah say
that a woman who gave birth brings an offering?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new אגדה about birth, separate from the זכר/נקבה wordplays.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the תורה obligates a יולדת to bring a קרבן.

steps.title: She swore during labor never to be with her husband
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי answers that in the pain of labor a woman swears never to be with her husband again, so she brings a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told them: When she crouches to give birth, she rushes to swear that she will never be with her husband again. That is why the תורה said she should bring a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי answers his students' question. The קרבן is connected to an oath the woman makes in the middle of labor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the pain is so strong, she quickly swears she will never be with her husband again. Later she goes back on that oath, so the תורה has her bring a קרבן for it.

keyTerms.meaning: Jumps up and swears, meaning she swears hastily
Be together (have relations) with her husband

phrases.english: He said to them:
At the time she crouches to give birth,
she jumps and swears
phrases.notes: 'Jumps' means she swears quickly, without thinking, because of the pain.

phrases.english: that she will not be with her husband,
therefore the Torah said she should bring an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the students' question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The יולדת brings a קרבן because during labor she rashly swore never to be with her husband again.

steps.title: רב יוסף: She broke the oath on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רבי שמעון בן יוחי. A woman who goes back to her husband breaks her oath deliberately, and an oath can be undone through regret anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: But she is acting on purpose! And the whole matter depends on regret!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the answer from Step 13, that the יולדת brings a קרבן because she broke her oath never to be with her husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן for a broken oath is brought only by someone who broke it by mistake (שוגג). This woman returns to her husband knowingly, so she is a מזיד, and no קרבן helps her. Also, if she wants out of the oath, she can regret it and have it released (חרטה), so there is no broken oath at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Acting on purpose, a deliberate violator
Regret, which can be used to release an oath

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב יוסף is denying that a יולדת brings a קרבן. That is a clear rule of the תורה. He is only attacking רבי שמעון בן יוחי's reason for it.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objects to this:
But she is acting on purpose,
and the matter depends on regret!
phrases.notes: He means she can regret the oath and have it released, so she never actually breaks it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון בן יוחי's reason that the יולדת's קרבן atones for a broken oath.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Oath קרבנות cover only accidental violation, and her oath can be released through regret. Either way, no oath-קרבן should apply.

steps.title: רב יוסף: The wrong kind of offering
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's second objection: if the קרבן were for a broken oath, she should bring the oath קרבן, not the special יולדת קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, she should need to bring an oath offering!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף adds a second problem to the same answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה has a specific קרבן for someone who breaks an oath (קרבן שבועה). The יולדת brings a different קרבן. So her קרבן cannot be the one for a broken oath. The גמרא does not answer these challenges here.

keyTerms.meaning: The offering brought for breaking an oath

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף gives two strong problems with the oath explanation: a deliberate violation gets no קרבן (and the oath can be released through regret), and the יולדת brings the wrong type of קרבן for an oath.

phrases.english: And furthermore —
she should need to bring an oath offering!
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'she needs'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to Step 14's attack.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the יולדת's קרבן is for her oath.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קרבן she actually brings does not match the קרבן the תורה requires for a broken oath.

steps.title: Why seven days for a boy and fourteen for a girl?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask רבי שמעון בן יוחי another question: why is a mother טמאה seven days after a boy but fourteen after a girl?
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what reason did the תורה say: a male, seven days, and a female, fourteen?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the students' list of questions to רבי שמעון בן יוחי. This one asks about the different number of days of טומאה after a birth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה sets seven days of טומאה after a boy and fourteen after a girl. The students want the reason behind the difference. The answer comes in the next step.

phrases.english: And for what reason did the Torah say
a male, for seven
and a female, for fourteen?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה זָכָר לְשִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יוסף's interruption, returns to the students' series of questions.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the difference between seven and fourteen days of טומאה.

steps.title: Joy over a boy makes her regret sooner
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי answers: everyone is happy about a boy, so the mother regrets her oath after seven days. Everyone is sad about a girl, so she regrets only after fourteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: A boy, whom everyone rejoices over, she regrets after seven. A girl, whom everyone is sad over, she regrets after fourteen.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי answers the question using the same idea of the oath from Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: How quickly the mother's mood recovers decides when she regrets her oath to stay away from her husband. The general joy at a boy's birth speeds this up. The tension around a girl's birth slows it down. The days of טומאה match that timing.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer is built on the oath idea that רב יוסף just challenged. The גמרא still brings it as רבי שמעון בן יוחי's teaching.

phrases.english: A male, over whom everyone rejoices —
she regrets after seven.
phrases.notes: She regrets the oath she made during labor, from Step 13.

phrases.english: A female, over whom everyone is sad —
she regrets after fourteen.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The days of טומאה match how long it takes the mother to regret her oath: sooner for a boy because of the joy, later for a girl.

steps.title: Why is מילה on the eighth day?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask why the תורה commands ברית מילה on the eighth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for what reason did the תורה say מילה on the eighth day?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask another 'why' question. This one is about the timing of ברית מילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question connects to the seven days of טומאה after a boy. The answer comes next.

phrases.english: And for what reason did the Torah say
circumcision on the eighth day?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 12:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה מִילָה לִשְׁמוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next question in the students' series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason ברית מילה is on the eighth day.

steps.title: So the parents are happy at the ברית too
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוחי answers: so that everyone won't be celebrating while the father and mother are sad.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that everyone should not be happy while his father and mother are sad.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן יוחי explains the eighth day with the seven days of טומאה after a boy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the first seven days, the parents are still forbidden to each other. A ברית during that time would mean everyone rejoices except the parents. On the eighth day they are permitted again, so they can share fully in the joy.

keyTerms.meaning: So that they should not be

phrases.english: So that everyone should not be happy
while his father and mother are sad.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ כּוּלָּם שְׂמֵחִים וְאָבִיו וְאִמּוֹ עֲצֵבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מילה is on the eighth day so the parents, now permitted to each other, can rejoice together with everyone.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון בן יוחי explains three rules about a יולדת with one idea: the oath she makes in labor and when she regrets it. That idea covers the קרבן, the seven or fourteen days, and מילה on the eighth day.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Why seven days of נדה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי מאיר's reason for the seven days of נדה: a husband who is always with his wife can grow tired of her. The seven days apart make her dear to him again, like on their wedding day.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי מאיר used to say: Why did the תורה say a נדה is for seven days? Because he gets used to her and becomes tired of her. The תורה said: let her be טמאה seven days, so that she will be as dear to her husband as when she entered the חופה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another 'why the תורה said' teaching, this time from רבי מאיר about נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a couple were never apart, closeness could turn into boredom and even dislike. The seven days of separation renew their relationship. Each time she becomes permitted again, she feels to her husband like a new bride.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her monthly period of separation
Used to her, too familiar with her
Tired of her, repulsed by her

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous teaching that explains the separation of נדה as something that protects and renews the marriage.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: the seven days of נדה keep the wife as dear to her husband as on their wedding day.

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Meir used to say:
For what reason did the Torah say
a menstruating woman for seven days?
Because he becomes used to her
phrases.notes: 'He' is the husband, if she were always permitted to him.

phrases.english: and grows tired of her.
The Torah said: 'Let her be impure seven days,'
so that she will be dear to her husband
as at the time she entered the wedding canopy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא הָיָה רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר מִפְּנֵי מָה אָמְרָה תּוֹרָה נִדָּה לְשִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching in the same style of 'why did the תורה say', now about נדה instead of a יולדת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The seven days of נדה exist so the wife stays as dear to her husband as on their wedding day.

steps.title: Why does a man pursue a woman?
steps.stepSummary: The students of רבי דוסתאי ברבי ינאי ask why the man is the one who searches for a wife, and not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: His students asked רבי דוסתאי ברבי ינאי: Why does a man go looking for a woman, but a woman does not go looking for a man?
steps.whatsHappening: A new set of questions begins, this time asked to a different teacher, רבי דוסתאי ברבי ינאי. The first question is why the man is usually the one who seeks out a wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This works like the earlier questions to רבי שמעון בן יוחי: students notice a pattern in everyday life and ask for its reason. The question sets up an answer that will go back to how man and woman were created.

keyTerms.meaning: Searches for, goes looking for (here: pursuing for marriage)

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: His students asked Rabbi Dostai son of Rabbi Yannai:

phrases.aramaic: מִפְּנֵי מָה אִישׁ מְחַזֵּר עַל אִשָּׁה,
phrases.english: Why does a man go searching for a woman,
but a woman does not go searching for a man?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ תַּלְמִידָיו אֶת רַבִּי דּוֹסְתַּאי בְּרַבִּי יַנַּאי מִפְּנֵי מָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new series of student questions, this time to רבי דוסתאי ברבי ינאי, after the earlier series to רבי שמעון בן יוחי and the ברייתא of רבי מאיר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason men pursue women for marriage and not the other way around.

steps.title: The owner searches for his lost item
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי answers with a parable: the one who lost something goes looking for it. The man 'lost' a part of himself when the woman was made from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like a person who lost something. Who looks for whom? The owner of the lost item looks for his lost item.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי answers the first question with a simple parable about a lost object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חוה was made from a part of אדם הראשון, so the man is like someone missing something of his own. The owner looks for the lost item, not the item for the owner, so the man is the one who searches.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner of the lost item

phrases.english: It is like a person who lost an item.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: Who searches for whom?
The owner of the lost item searches for his lost item.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The man is like an owner searching for his lost object, since the woman was taken from him.

steps.title: Why do man and woman face different directions?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask why, during intimacy, the man faces down and the woman faces up toward him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does a man face downward, and a woman faces upward toward the man?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask a second question, about the way husband and wife face during intimacy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the students point to a difference between men and women and ask for its reason. The answer will again go back to creation.

phrases.english: And why does a man face downward,
phrases.notes: He is talking about husband and wife during intimacy.

phrases.english: and a woman faces upward, toward the man?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the man faces down and the woman faces up toward him.

steps.title: Each faces where they came from
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי answers: the man faces the earth he was made from, and the woman faces the man she was made from.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one faces the place he was created from, and that one faces the place she was created from.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי answers the second question by pointing to where each one was created from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדם הראשון was formed from the ground, so the man faces down toward the earth. חוה was formed from אדם, so the woman faces up toward the man. This short answer becomes the pattern for the next two answers too.

keyTerms.meaning: From the place where he was created

steps.whatToRemember: The key line 'זה ממקום שנברא וזו ממקום שנבראת' is the main idea of this whole section: the man came from earth and the woman came from the man, and that explains their differences.

phrases.english: This one faces the place he was created from,
and that one faces the place she was created from.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁנִּבְרָא וְזוֹ מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁנִּבְרֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Each one faces their place of origin: the man faces the earth, and the woman faces the man.

steps.title: Why is a man easier to calm down?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask why an angry man accepts appeasement more easily than a woman does.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why does a man accept being calmed down, but a woman does not accept being calmed down?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask a third question, about why a man is more easily calmed after being upset.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question compares how men and women respond when someone tries to make peace with them. The answer will use the same creation formula as before, with a new meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: Appeasement, being calmed down or made up with
Accepts appeasement, lets himself be calmed

phrases.english: And why does a man accept appeasement,
but a woman does not accept appeasement?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a man is more easily appeased than a woman.

steps.title: Soft earth versus hard bone
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי gives the same answer: each acts like what they were made from. Earth gives way, but bone stays firm.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is like the place he was created from, and that one is like the place she was created from.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי answers the third question with the exact same words as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the words carry a new meaning. The man came from earth, which is soft and can be shaped, so he softens easily. The woman came from a bone, which is hard and does not bend, so she stays firm.
steps.confusionAlert: The words are identical to step 24, but they do not mean the same thing. There they meant 'facing' the place of creation. Here they mean 'acting like' the material of creation, soft earth versus hard bone.

phrases.english: This one is like the place he was created from,
phrases.notes: Earth is soft and gives way when pressed.

phrases.english: and that one is like the place she was created from.
phrases.notes: She came from a bone, which is hard and does not bend easily.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁנִּבְרָא וְזוֹ מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁנִּבְרֵאת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 with the same formula used in step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The man acts like soft earth and gives in; the woman acts like hard bone and does not.

steps.title: Why is a woman's voice pleasant?
steps.stepSummary: The students ask why a woman's voice is pleasant and a man's voice is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is a woman's voice pleasant, but a man's voice is not pleasant?
steps.whatsHappening: The students ask their fourth and last question in this series, about the sound of men's and women's voices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is another everyday difference between men and women. The answer will once more go back to creation, and this time it will be backed by a פסוק.

phrases.english: Why is a woman's voice pleasant,
but a man's voice is not pleasant?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth question in the same series.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a woman's voice is pleasant and a man's is not.

steps.title: Bone rings, earth is silent, with a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי דוסתאי again answers from creation and brings a פסוק from שיר השירים that praises a woman's sweet voice.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is like the place he was created from, and that one is like the place she was created from, as it says: 'For your voice is sweet and your appearance is lovely.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי דוסתאי answers the last question with the same creation formula and adds a פסוק to show that a woman's voice is pleasant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earth makes no sound when you hit it, but a bone gives off a sound. So the man, made from earth, does not have a ringing voice, while the woman, made from bone, does. The פסוק from שיר השירים supports the idea that a woman's voice is sweet.

keyTerms.meaning: Song of Songs, the book the פסוק comes from

steps.whatToRemember: All four of רבי דוסתאי's answers come from one idea: man was made from earth, and woman was made from the man's bone. Each one's nature matches the material they came from.

phrases.english: This one is like the place he was created from,
phrases.notes: Earth makes no sound when it is struck.

phrases.english: and that one is like the place she was created from,
phrases.notes: A bone makes a sound when it is struck.

phrases.english: as it is said:
"For your voice is sweet, and your appearance is lovely."
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 2:14.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁנִּבְרָא וְזוֹ מִמְּקוֹם שֶׁנִּבְרֵאת שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 and closes the series of questions to רבי דוסתאי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The woman, made from bone, has a ringing and pleasant voice. The man, made from silent earth, does not. A פסוק in שיר השירים praises a woman's sweet voice.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of המפלת חתיכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally ends the third פרק of מסכת נדה, called המפלת חתיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter "המפלת חתיכה."
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. It is the standard closing line that marks the end of the פרק המפלת חתיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every פרק in ש"ס ends with a הדרן line, a promise to come back and learn it again. The name of the פרק comes from its first words. The next line starts a brand-new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: "We will return to you": the closing formula said at the end of a פרק
"A woman who miscarries a piece of tissue": the name of the third פרק of נדה

steps.whatToRemember: The פרק המפלת חתיכה is now finished. A new topic begins right after this line.

phrases.english: We will return to you, chapter "One who miscarries a piece of tissue."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the whole פרק, which ended with רבי דוסתאי's answers about creation (steps 24–28).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק המפלת חתיכה is complete.

steps.title: Samaritan girls are נדות from the cradle, and Samaritan men make lower bedding impure
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that daughters of כותים are treated as נדות from infancy. It also rules that כותים men make the bedding under them impure like the top layer, because they are בועלי נדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Daughters of כותים are considered נדות from their cradle. And כותים men make the lower bedding impure just like the upper bedding, because they are men who have relations with נדות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה that sets two rules about כותים. Their girls are treated as נדות even as babies, and their men make the bedding beneath them impure the way a בועל נדה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule 'משכב תחתון כעליון' is the standard rule for any בועל נדה. The bedding under him gets the same level of impurity as the bedding lying on top of a זב, which makes food and drink impure. What is new here is that the משנה gives all כותים men the status of בועלי נדות. The next line explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: Samaritans: a group whose observance of some הלכות was not trusted
Considered נדות from their cradle, meaning even as babies
The lower bedding is like the upper: the layers underneath are impure like bedding on top of a זב
Men who have relations with women who are נדות

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה does not say that every כותית baby actually has a flow. It sets a status for them. The גמרא will soon ask how this can make sense.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Daughters of Samaritans
are menstruating women from their cradle.
And the Samaritan men make impure
the lower bedding like the upper bedding,
phrases.notes: He means the layers under him get the same level of impurity as bedding lying on top of a זב.

phrases.english: because they are men who have relations with menstruating women.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new פרק right after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daughters of כותים are נדות from the cradle. כותים men make the lower bedding impure like the upper bedding, since they are בועלי נדות.

steps.title: Why כותים are considered בועלי נדות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains that כותים women count seven days from every flow of blood. Because of this, their count can be wrong, and their husbands may be with them while they are still נדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they (the women) sit for every single flow of blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the reason behind the label בועלי נדות from the last step. כותים women start a seven-day count from any blood at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sounds strict, but it causes a problem. If a truly impure flow comes in the middle of a count that began with clean blood, they keep counting from the first blood and finish too early. So their husbands may be with them while they are really still נדות.

keyTerms.meaning: Every single flow of blood, even blood that does not make a woman impure

steps.confusionAlert: Being stricter here does not help. Counting from the wrong blood can make the seven days end too early, and that is the real problem.

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵן יוֹשְׁבוֹת עַל כׇּל דָּם וָדָם.
phrases.english: And they sit (seven days) for each and every blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵן יוֹשְׁבוֹת עַל כׇּל דָּם וָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason for calling כותים בועלי נדות in step 30.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותים women keep seven days for every blood, so their count can be wrong and their husbands become בועלי נדות.

steps.title: The impurity of כותים is only a doubt, so no punishment and no burning of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה limits its own ruling. Since the impurity of כותים is only a ספק, one is not liable for entering the מקדש because of it, and תרומה that touched it is not burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one is not liable for entering the מקדש because of them, and one does not burn תרומה because of them, since their impurity is a doubt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now limits the strict rules it just gave. The impurity of כותים is only a doubt, so the most serious results do not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Entering the מקדש while impure makes a person liable to bring a קרבן, and impure תרומה must be burned. Both of these apply only to certain impurity. Because the impurity of כותים is a ספק, they treat it as impure but do not apply these consequences.

keyTerms.meaning: Entering the מקדש, which is forbidden while impure
Burning תרומה, which is done when it is surely impure
Their impurity is only a doubt

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה about כותים has three parts. Their girls are נדות from the cradle. Their men make even the lower bedding impure. But because it is all a ספק, there is no liability for the מקדש and no burning of תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a basic pattern in הלכה. A doubtful impurity can call for caution, but it does not trigger the strongest results, like a קרבן or burning תרומה.

phrases.english: But one is not liable because of them
for entering the Temple,
and one does not burn teruma because of them,
because their impurity is uncertain.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין חַיָּיבִין עֲלֵיהֶן עַל בִּיאַת מִקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the strict rules of steps 30–31 by saying the impurity is only a ספק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the impurity of כותים is a ספק, one is not liable for entering the מקדש because of it, and תרומה is not burned because of it.

steps.title: What case is the משנה talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule about the daughters of כותים with a two-sided question: either way, the rule seems not to make sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the case? If they see blood, then even our girls should be impure too. And if they do not see blood, then their girls should not be impure either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the new משנה by asking what situation it means when it calls the daughters of כותים נדות from infancy. It shows that both possible readings seem to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a young girl actually sees blood, she is a נדה whether she is Jewish or a כותית, so the משנה would not need to single out כותים. If she does not see blood, there is no reason to call her a נדה at all. So the special rule for כותים seems to have no case where it fits.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? A question asking for the exact situation.
They see blood, meaning they have a menstrual flow.
Theirs, meaning the girls of the כותים.

phrases.english: גמרא: What are the circumstances?
If they actually see blood,
then even ours as well [would be impure],
and if they do not see blood,
then theirs should not [be impure] either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion of the משנה's rule from step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that the daughters of כותים are נדות from infancy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided challenge: if they see blood, the rule should apply to Jewish girls too; if they do not, it should not apply even to כותים.

steps.title: The משנה means an unknown case, and we worry about the minority
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the משנה is talking about girls about whom it is unknown whether they have seen blood. Since some girls do, we are concerned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא the son of רב אחא בר רב הונא said in the name of רב ששת: What are we dealing with here? An unknown case. Since there is a minority of girls who see blood, we are concerned.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת resolves the challenge. The משנה is not talking about girls known to see blood or known not to. It is talking about girls whose status is unknown.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This introduces a third option the challenge did not consider: the unknown case. Most young girls do not see blood, but a minority do, so we treat each girl of the כותים as though she might belong to that minority. This answer only works if we worry about a minority instead of following the majority, which is what the next step asks about.

keyTerms.meaning: What are we dealing with here? Introduces a specific case that resolves a difficulty.
An unknown case, where we do not know the facts.
We are concerned, so we act strictly because of a possibility.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַחָא בַּר רַב הוּנָא

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge of step 33.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case as a third, unknown situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenge assumed the girls either definitely see blood or definitely do not.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is talking about an unknown case, and we are strict because a minority of girls do see blood.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the משנה's rule rests on worrying about a minority, which the גמרא is about to examine.

steps.title: Which תנא worries about a minority?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that one must be concerned about a minority, since רב ששת's answer depends on that idea.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who is concerned about a minority?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It asks which תנא holds the view that a minority must be taken into account.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually we follow the majority, and most young girls do not see blood. Since רב ששת's answer requires worrying about the minority, the גמרא wants to find the תנא who holds that view and tie the משנה to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage of the משנה period.
Is concerned about the minority, rather than relying only on the majority.
